text: At 65', Seabrook Town implemented a pressing trigger by increasing press intensity from 0.66 to 0.84 and raising their defensive line height from 0.6 to 0.72, aiming to disrupt Harbour City's patient short passing in their 4-2-3-1 setup [#1361]. Concurrently, they shifted to a more direct attacking mechanism, increasing their directness metric from 0.42 to 0.57 to exploit wide crossing opportunities inherent in their 3-4-3 formation [#1361]. These adjustments elevated their expected goals from 0.45 to 0.61 and marginally increased possession (53.6% to 54.4%) but reduced field tilt from 71.4% to 47.8%, indicating Harbour City regained some territorial advantage despite the heightened press [#1361]. The combination of a higher line and intensified pressing (PPDA dropping from 6.0 to 5.8) facilitated more aggressive ball recoveries in advanced areas, although box touches slightly decreased from 9 to 8, suggesting a trade-off between territorial control and direct penetration [#1361].
